## What & why

On libstdc++, the shortest-number search can serialize the largest finite binary64 value as `2e+308`. Parsing that candidate saturates to `DBL_MAX` and sets the stream failure flag, but the equality-only check accepts it. A finite JSON value therefore becomes an overflowing representation.

Reject failed round trips that saturated to the maximum finite magnitude and continue searching at higher precision. Keep valid subnormal round trips: libc++ can set the failure flag for subnormal underflow even when the parsed value is correct, so rejecting every failed stream would change existing valid output.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

- [Linux/libstdc++ validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43930624772): reproduced the original `DBL_MAX` failure, then passed **1,030 ordered-JSON comparisons and rejection cases** with this exact fix.
- [macOS/libc++ validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43928604436/job/133514659142): **101 L0/L1 tests passed, 3 Vulkan tests skipped**, and all 1,030 JSON comparisons passed. This includes the smallest signed subnormals as compatibility controls.
- Added positive and negative maximum finite values, their finite neighbors, minimum normal values, signed subnormals, and rejection controls just above the finite range to the existing Python-oracle test, alongside its 1,000 seeded random finite values.
- Local Linux JSON comparisons passed. The full local L0/L1 command also ran in the development checkout, which contains separate cache-accounting and asset-checker changes: **99 passed, 3 skipped**, with the previously reproduced sandbox `std::tmpfile` and Linux platform-memory test failures remaining. ## What & why

A desktop chat can receive the terminal `data: [DONE]` event while the HTTP response remains open. The client currently waits for transport EOF, keeping the request active until cancellation. It also continues parsing subsequent frames, which can alter the completed answer or raise a JSON error.

Stop consuming the stream at its terminal event and release the reader through the existing cleanup path. Ignore further accumulator input after completion. The regressions cover whole and byte-fragmented responses, retained answer/usage data, reader cancellation, and trailing frames.

## Area

- [x] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)

## How was it tested?

On Linux, Node 24.15.0 and 26.3.1 each reproduced all four new failures against upstream `f6bfa55`, then passed **218 frontend tests** and `npm run build` with this change.

[Before/after validation and full logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43928618071).

The same jobs exercised the real Node HTTP server and native `fetch`: the server sent content, usage, and `[DONE]` without closing the response. Upstream remained active until the 500 ms abort deadline; the fixed client completed in 4.8–6.2 ms with the same answer and metrics. This measures completion of that specific protocol reproduction, not inference performance.

Local Node 24.22.1 also passed all 218 tests, the TypeScript/Vite build, and the native HTTP reproduction.

## What & why

`generation_config.json` uses JSON's decimal point, but the native reader converts floating values with `std::stod`, which follows the embedding application's current numeric locale. With a German locale, a valid temperature of `0.625` becomes `0`, changing the sampling configuration.

Give each parser its own C numeric locale and use the platform's locale-specific conversion (`strtod_l` or `_strtod_l`). This keeps the existing native range handling, including underflow and overflow, without changing the process locale. Unknown provider fields continue to be ignored when their numeric values are outside the supported range.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

The production branch contains the same two source/test files as validation commit `62855b4e87f5a42a8d3a98954f5bef29308e1c02`.

- [Linux native validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43955376404/job/133608432523): the original implementation fails the real configuration test with German `0.625` becoming `0`; the revised generation-defaults and model-catalog tests pass. The changed source also compiles against Android API 28.
- [Windows/MSVC native validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43955376404/job/133608432586): the same original-source failure and revised-source success were reproduced with native Windows binaries.
- The regression compares 13 numeric inputs with that platform's original C-locale `std::stod` behavior, including signed zero, binary64 boundaries, subnormal inputs, underflow and overflow. It also checks ignored provider fields and 800 concurrent configuration reads per available locale, verifying that the process locale remains unchanged.
- Local Linux: the two affected tests pass in C, German and French locales after reproducing the original failure. Commands: `cmake --build --preset cpu --target moe_test_model_generation_defaults moe_test_model_catalog` and `ctest --preset cpu --output-on-failure -R '^moe_test_model_(generation_defaults|catalog)$'`.

**Validation blockers:** This branch is not ready for review. The [complete Linux L0/L1 comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43958711925/job/133620460669) completed and failed: the revised generation-defaults test passes, but the platform headers added to `src/model/asset_index.cpp` introduce a new `check_layers` failure. The revised suite has 97 runnable passes, 3 device skips and 4 failures. The other three failures (`moe_test_platform_memory`, `moe_test_ordered_json`, `moe_test_template_tools`) were reproduced with the original parser in the same job; the unchanged weights test also failed 4 of 100 baseline repetitions. ## What & why

The delegated engine can report a protocol error after HTTP 200 stream headers have been sent. The proxy forwards that error correctly, but loses its diagnostic fields when recording the request. Chat and Messages then show `stop_reason: unknown`; Responses keeps `failed` but loses the error code. This makes `/status` and recent request history incomplete when diagnosing engine failures.

Retain the error's `code` (falling back to `type`), `message` and `param`, and record the terminal reason as `failed`. The HTTP status and all forwarded bytes remain unchanged. Successful Responses objects with `error: null` retain their normal completion status.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

The [isolated native before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43945833532/job/133575120819) tests the exact production changes and regressions in this PR against upstream `f6bfa5546bcf89919f86946ec669bcc7f4cd526d`.

## What & why

An asynchronous weight read retains its allocation in the packaged-task closure. Its future can become ready before that closure is destroyed, so `complete()` followed by `close()` can leave the resident-weight budget charged until the worker releases its task. The existing mixed-storage test also intermittently encounters this residual charge.

Move the worker's allocation reference into a local lifetime guard when the task starts. It keeps the buffer alive throughout the read and releases the reference before the task publishes its result, including an error return or exception. Add a regression that completes, checks the loaded bytes and closes 1,000 small weight loads, checking that no completed load retains a resident charge.

# Contributing to edge0

Thanks for your interest in contributing! edge0 is an open-source streaming MoE
inference framework, and contributions of all kinds are welcome — bug reports,
performance measurements, documentation fixes, new model support, and new
platform/backend work.

## Ways to contribute

- **Report a bug / performance issue / request a feature or model** — open an
  issue using one of the [issue forms](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/). The forms ask
  for the platform, backend, chip and memory — these fields resolve the large
  majority of reports, so please fill them in.
- **Ask a question or share results** — please use
  [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Edge0/discussions) rather
  than an issue.
- **Send a pull request** — see the workflow below.

## Repository layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| [`edge0-infer/`](edge0-infer/) | The program you run: the native inference engine (C++, GGML), its CLI and local OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible server, the model asset tools, and the chat app examples for desktop, Android and iOS |
| [`edge0-strata/`](edge0-strata/EDGE0.md) | The engine for `edge0-145b` and `edge0-120b` (NVIDIA GPU on Linux or Windows, Metal on macOS), a fork of Strata that `edge0-infer` starts for these models |
| [`docs/`](docs/) | Model design docs: MoE routing, the prerouter, and the model tiers |
| [`paper/`](paper/) | The technical report |

`edge0-infer/` is developed in a separate repository and synced here. Open
issues and pull requests for it in this repository as usual: an accepted change
is applied there first and arrives here with the next sync.

## Development setup

Build the engine and get the model assets as described in
[Getting started](edge0-infer/docs/getting-started.md). It covers macOS, iOS,
Android, Linux and Windows. For `edge0-145b` and `edge0-120b`, also build
`edge0-strata/` as [`edge0-strata/EDGE0.md`](edge0-strata/EDGE0.md) describes.

## Running the tests

The tests are CTest tests with a level label from `L0` (static checks) to `L4`
(acceptance on a device). From `edge0-infer/`:

```bash
cmake --preset cpu && cmake --build --preset cpu
ctest --preset cpu -L "L0|L1"     # no model assets needed
```

[Testing](edge0-infer/docs/testing.md) describes every level, what each needs
(the tiny test fixtures, the real assets, a device) and the full regression
commands.

## Adding a new model

A model has two parts in `edge0-infer/`: its asset tools in
`edge0-infer/tools/assets/<model>/` (see
[Adding a model](edge0-infer/tools/assets/README.md#adding-a-model)) and its
computation in `edge0-infer/src/models/<model>/` (see
[Architecture](edge0-infer/docs/architecture.md)). Please include a short note
on the architecture (layers / experts / routing width / attention type) in your
PR.

## Pull request workflow

1. **Fork** the repo and create a feature branch off `main`
   (e.g. `fix/expert-slot-oob`, `docs/clarify-memory`, `feat/tool-calling`).
2. Make your change; **add or update tests** for new behavior.
3. Run the tests for the levels your change touches (at least `L0` and `L1`)
   locally.
4. Open a PR against `Edge0-AI/Edge0:main` and fill in the
   [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Link the issue it closes
   (`Fixes #NN`).
5. Keep PRs focused — one logical change per PR is easier to review and merge.

### Commit / PR style

This repo uses conventional-commit-style prefixes, e.g.
`fix(experts): ...`, `feat(server): ...`, `docs(readme): ...`,
`perf(decode): ...`, `chore: ...`. Please follow the same convention.

## Reporting security issues

Do not open a public issue for security problems. Email **samuel@edge0.ai**
instead.

## License

By contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the
project's [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) license. Contributions to `edge0-strata/` are
licensed under that directory's [MIT](edge0-strata/LICENSE) license.

# Contributing to Strata

**AI assistance is welcome. The contributor is responsible for understanding the change and supplying real evidence.**

These rules apply to issues, pull requests, benchmark reports, and the agents helping prepare them.
You should be able to explain every changed line and answer review questions about it.

## Before starting

1. Search [issues](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues) and
   [pull requests](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pulls), including closed discussions. Add new evidence to an
   existing thread when it covers your problem.
2. Read [EDGE0.md](EDGE0.md) and the documentation for the component you want to change.
3. Get maintainer agreement on scope before substantial features, refactors, architecture changes, or changes to
   defaults. Describe the user problem, proposed behavior, and tradeoffs in an issue first. Agreement on scope
   does not guarantee a merge. Focused fixes and benchmark reports can go straight to a PR.
4. Keep one problem per PR. Update that PR after feedback; do not open competing attempts for the same change.

Do not resubmit a declined proposal under a different title or through another agent. If new evidence changes
the situation, bring it to the original discussion and let a maintainer decide whether to reopen it.

## Report a problem people can investigate

Use the matching [issue form](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/new/choose). A bug report should include:

- The smallest steps or command that reproduce the problem, and the expected and actual behavior.
- Strata version or commit, OS, GPU and VRAM, and relevant model, quantization, and configuration.
- The exact error and relevant logs, with credentials and private content removed.
- Whether you reproduced it yourself. Label a finding based only on reading code or a scanner as
  **unconfirmed static analysis**, and explain the suspected path without presenting it as an observed failure.

Do not invent reproduction steps, errors, affected hardware, or severity. If you cannot reproduce something,
say what you inspected and what would verify the hypothesis. Feature requests should explain a concrete user
need and the current workaround. Questions should say what you tried and where you got stuck.

Example structure, with placeholders to replace with actual observations:

```text
Problem: <one observed behavior>
Environment: <commit, OS, GPU/VRAM, model/quant, relevant settings>
Reproduce: <exact command or short sequence>
Expected: <documented or intended behavior>
Actual: <observed behavior and exact error>
Evidence: <sanitized log attachment>
Reproduction status: <reproduced locally OR unconfirmed static analysis>
```

## Titles

Every issue and pull request title starts with its area in square brackets, then a short description: `[Engine]`, `[GUI]`, `[TUI]`,
`[Benchmark]`, `[Docs]` or `[Other]`. For example `[Engine] fix decode stop on long prompts` or `[GUI] keep the model list after a tab
switch`. The issue forms ask for the area and a check on the title fails when the prefix is missing.

## Prepare a focused pull request

Lead with the problem and resulting behavior. Explain why the approach is needed, the important limits, and
any compatibility effects. Link the issue and scope agreement when applicable. A file-by-file narration or
an AI-generated summary of the diff is not a substitute for this explanation.

- Keep unrelated formatting, cleanup, dependency changes, and speculative abstractions out of the PR.
- Add documentation where it changes what a user or developer needs to know. Avoid repeated summaries,
  speculative roadmaps, and generated documentation with no actionable information.
- Preserve existing behavior outside the intended change. New features are opt-in and must not
  slow down or change the default path.
- Read the complete diff, including generated files, before submitting. Remove debugging output, secrets,
  private paths, and accidental files.
- Prefer a small relevant regression check over tests that only restate the implementation. Documentation-only
  changes need link, example, and consistency checks; they do not require GPU builds.

## Show the validation you actually performed

List exact commands, the revision and environment tested, and observed outcomes. Keep **passed**, **failed**,
and **not run** separate. Include relevant output or a log attachment. A command you suggest running is not
evidence that it passed; a CI run on a different revision is not validation of the submitted code.

Build every backend a code change touches, including CUDA, HIP, and SYCL where applicable, before requesting
review. For changes that need hardware execution, report that execution separately from compilation. A mock,
static check, or successful build does not establish hardware correctness. If you lack a required environment,
keep the PR as a draft, identify the missing checks, and ask for targeted help in the same thread. Do not claim
compatibility you have not tested.

Performance claims need before/after runs on the same hardware and workload, with every changed setting
identified. Preserve the individual runs, failures, and variability. Follow the
[community measurement guide](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md); standard submissions will use the
[benchmark protocol](docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md) once it is activated. One fast run does not justify changing a
default or claiming a speedup for other machines.

Example PR body; placeholders are not test results:

```text
Problem and result: <trigger; behavior before and after the change>
Related discussion: <issue URL and scope agreement, when required>
Approach: <why this fix; relevant compatibility effects>
Validation:
  Passed: <exact command, revision/environment, observed result, log>
  Failed: <exact command and failure, or none observed>
  Not run: <check, reason, and what remains unverified>
Limits: <known limitations or remaining work>
```

## Rules for AI-assisted work

Use agents to help investigate, implement, and explain work that you can review. Before submitting, verify
their claims against the source, actual command output, or a cited primary reference.

Never submit fabricated measurements, invented test results, fake logs, or copied claims you have not checked.
Do not turn a repository scan into a batch of speculative issues or PRs. Consolidate related findings, establish
their effect, and submit the useful evidence. Do not present an agent's confidence or another model's approval
as validation. Keep review replies concise and address the requested change or evidence directly.

Maintainers may request a smaller change, return a PR to draft, or close a submission that lacks evidence,
duplicates existing work, or ignores agreed scope. A smaller, understandable contribution with honest limits
is easier to review and maintain.

## Share a benchmark

A results-only PR should contain the human report, raw measurements, sanitized configuration, and supporting
logs. Keep it separate from engine changes and include poor results and failed requests.

The [current community benchmark guide](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md) remains available for measurements made
with today's tools. The [new protocol](docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md) defines the draft standard and future approval
workflow. Its draft status must remain visible: existing reports are not automatically standard or approved.

Run the launch commands below from `edge0-infer/`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Edge0.git edge0 ``` - **edge0-strata**, the engine: follow "Build (Linux, NVIDIA)", "Build (Windows, NVIDIA)" or "Build (macOS, Apple Silicon)" in [edge0-strata/EDGE0.md](edge0-strata/EDGE0.md). - **edge0-infer**: follow "Build" (Linux) or "Windows" in [edge0-infer/docs/getting-started.md](edge0-infer/docs/getting-started.md). **2. Run from the command line.** Pass one model folder, such as `Edge0-145B-q3k`, not the folder that holds several of them. On Windows the program is `build\windows\bin\edge0-infer.exe`. ```bash build/cpu/bin/edge0-infer serve --model /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k ``` It prints `Listening: http://127.0.0.1:8000 model=` once the weights are loaded, where `` is `edge0_145b`, and then serves OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints: ```bash curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"edge0_145b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":64}' ``` `edge0-infer chat --model /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k` opens an interactive session instead. More options: [edge0-infer/docs/edge0-145b.md](edge0-infer/docs/edge0-145b.md).
Two GPUs · a second card's expert tier A second NVIDIA card holds the experts that do not fit in the first one's VRAM, and decoding uses it for both expert formats. The cards need no NVLink or P2P. `edge0-infer` runs the engine on one card (its `--device` is one card), so for two cards start the engine with the config `serve/server.py --config` reads (it holds `exe`, `args`, `cwd`, `env`): - set `"gpu": [0, 1]` — the engine's device 0 is the first card, device 1 the second; - append to `"args"`: `"--peer-device", "1", "--peer-reserve-mib", "1024", "--peer-slots", "0"`. ```bash cd /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k /path/to/edge0-strata/.venv/bin/python /path/to/edge0-strata/serve/server.py \ --engine strata --config ./model-two-gpus.json ``` The startup log prints the second card's tier (`peer GPU 1: … experts, … GiB`), and the server serves the same endpoints as on one card. `--peer-device` cannot be combined with `--layer-split` or `--expert-cache-device1..3`. More: [Two GPUs](edge0-strata/EDGE0.md#two-gpus-linux-nvidia).
Desktop app · Windows · macOS ⬇️ **Download:** **[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Edge0/releases)** Open **Edge0 Chat** on Windows or macOS (Apple Silicon) and choose a model folder, such as `Edge0-145B-q3k`, to run the model locally. To build the app from source, follow the [Edge0 Chat](edge0-infer/examples/desktop/README.md) guide.
Images · vision `mmproj-BF16.gguf` in the model folder is the vision encoder. Add this to the model's `model.json`, next to `args`: ```json "vision": {"exe": "/path/to/strata-vision", "mmproj": "./mmproj-BF16.gguf", "model": "./model-skeleton.gguf", "gpu": false} ``` and `--vision` to `"args"`. `strata-vision` is not in this repository: `setup.py --setup --vision yes` fetches it, or build `tools/vision` in a Strata checkout. The log then says `images on`; send a picture with `/image` in the chat, or an `image_url` part over the OpenAI API.
## Usage & troubleshooting 145B / 120B · Memory options
Low RAM · SSD offload - **SSD mode:** `--mmap-experts` — read uncached experts from SSD on demand. - **Low-memory arguments:** ```bash --resident-budget-gib 20 --expert-profile expert-profile.bin ``` Up to **20 GiB** of host RAM for the expert cache; uncached experts are read from SSD on demand. Includes `--mmap-experts` and disjoint GPU/RAM caches automatically. **Required:** a static expert profile. Replace `expert-profile.bin` with your profile path.
RAM budget · what 20 GiB covers - **Expert cache:** `--resident-budget-gib 20` caps host-RAM expert caching at **20 GiB**, lowered further to fit available memory. - **Total RAM:** expert cache + other runtime allocations. This flag does **not** set a total-process RAM limit. - **Benchmark limit:** the 20 GiB total RAM test budget is a separate measurement condition.
GPU / RAM · avoid duplicate experts - **Enable:** `--resident-experts` or `--resident-budget-gib N`, with a static `--expert-profile`. - **Effect:** experts cached in VRAM need no duplicate RAM copy. Compatible with SSD loading. - **Default:** off, prioritizing speed. - **Automatically enabled:** `--mmap-experts`, `--resident-cpu-experts`, `--resident-pin`.
### Capacity controls · VRAM and host RAM These live in the pack's `model.json` (`args` for flags, `env` for environment variables), so a change there applies to every launch of the model. | Flag | Meaning | Default | |---|---|---| | `--vram-reserve-mib N` | VRAM left free for the desktop, the driver and other processes; the engine sizes its caches from what remains. | `700` | | `--expert-cache N\|auto` | Expert slots kept in VRAM. `auto` derives the count from the free VRAM after the fixed footprint (projections, MTP draft, verify buffers, D/U device buffers). | `0` | | `--kv-resident N` | KV cells kept in VRAM per QSA layer; the rest streams from pinned host RAM, which frees VRAM for experts. | `0` | | `--spec N` | The MTP drafter's verify window: tokens proposed per check. A bigger window needs bigger verify buffers (about 180 MiB at 4) and pays off when every window has a fixed per-layer cost. Without an MTP layer there is no speculation. | `4` | | `--resident-budget-gib N` | Cap on the host-RAM expert cache. It holds only the experts the VRAM cache does **not** hold, so the two sets are disjoint, and the value is clamped to the RAM available minus headroom. ## Roadmap
Q4 2026 · architecture and inference **Models & algorithms** Q4 works two fronts: bringing a next-generation architecture into the framework, and turning latent reasoning into a real latency saving rather than just an arithmetic one. - **Next-gen architecture support (Qwen3.8-Flash class)** — run hybrid linear attention (GDN + QSA), gated multi-branch residual, and N-gram embedding topologies on edge0. These designs suit SSD streaming offload naturally: O(1)-state attention keeps long thinking from becoming a KV-cache problem, and lookup-only N-gram tables stream on demand. Goal: the tier runs on a single device and benchmarks within an acceptable gap of the fp16 base. - **Latent thinking + batched expert pre-prediction** — make latent reasoning a *latency* saving, not only an arithmetic one. The core engineering problem: move expert routing from per-position to **once per block**, so one prediction covers every position and round of a block and **expert load volume decouples from the reasoning loop count** — plus cross-block prefetch that loads the next block's experts inside the current block's compute window. Progress is measured as **end-to-end thinking-phase time at matched accuracy** (never tokens/s). [Previous-release milestones and planned native-engine support](docs/legacy-models.md#roadmap).

# Testing

The tests are CTest tests. Each one carries a level label, `L0` to `L4`, ordered from cheapest to most expensive; tests that need a GPU or other device also carry the label `device`. Every property is tested at the cheapest level that can decide it.

## Levels

| Level | What it checks | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `L0` static | Public headers compile on their own, language and documentation checks, dependency and layering rules, vendored source checks. Runs in a few seconds. | Nothing |
| `L1` unit | Pure logic: tokenizer, prefix matching, sampling, slot selection, CLI parsing, the asset and measurement tools | The Python environment of the asset tools |
| `L2` integration | Several modules together on a tiny random-weight model with the same structure as the 35B; single-turn computation is compared with the reference answers in [`tests/fixtures/answers/`](../tests/fixtures/answers/README.md) | `$MOE_TINY`; `$MOE_SOURCE_35B` for the asset tools' fixture test |
| `L3` real assets | The 35B on real assets: logits, routing, expert loads, memory peaks | `$MOE_ASSETS_35B` |
| `L4` acceptance | Fixed scenarios through the CLI only, per platform | `$MOE_ASSETS_35B`, the target device |

`L3`, `L4` and `device` tests run one at a time even when CTest runs others in parallel, because they assert memory peaks or share the GPU. A test that cannot run in the current environment, such as a Metal test without a Metal device or a check that needs Git metadata, exits with code 77 and is reported as skipped, not as passed.

## Setup

1. Create the Python environment that the Python tests use (it lives in the ignored `tools/assets/.venv`):

   ```sh
   uv sync --project tools/assets
   ```

2. For `L2`, generate the tiny fixtures as described in the [asset tools guide](../tools/assets/README.md#tiny-fixtures) and export their directory as `MOE_TINY`. This needs only three small text files of the 35B source, not the full weights; keep `MOE_SOURCE_35B` exported: the asset tools' fixture test needs it and is otherwise skipped.
3. For `L3` and `L4`, convert the 35B as described in [Getting started](getting-started.md#get-a-model) and export `MOE_ASSETS_35B`.

## Running

```sh
cmake --preset cpu && cmake --build --preset cpu
ctest --preset cpu -L "L0|L1"                                    # no assets needed
ctest --preset cpu --no-tests=error -L "L0|L1|L2" -LE device     # with $MOE_TINY

cmake --preset mac-metal && cmake --build --preset mac-metal
ctest --preset mac-metal --no-tests=error -L "device|L3"         # Metal and real assets
```

These commands, with both presets built, are the full regression on macOS. Tests are registered only when `MOE_BUILD_TESTS` is ON, the default when this repository is the top-level project; it defaults to OFF when the repository is [added to another CMake project](getting-started.md#use-from-another-cmake-project). `ctest -N -L <level>` lists the tests of a level without running them.

`tools/run_checks.py` configures, builds and runs the chosen levels in one step and lists every test as passed, failed or not executed, with the reason:

```sh
uv run --no-project python -I tools/run_checks.py --preset cpu --levels L0,L1,L2
```

## Platform and performance tests

- [Platform CLI scenarios](../tests/platform/README.md) run the `L4` scenarios on Android and iOS devices, through wrappers that stand in for `edge0-infer` on the host, and on Windows directly.
- [Measurement tools](../tests/perf/README.md) produce the performance reports described in [Benchmarking](benchmarking.md); measurements are not part of the test levels.

# Source checks

These checks catch accidental dependency and layering mistakes. They are not
intended to prevent deliberate evasion.

- CMake checks inspect literal commands only; they do not interpret variables,
  functions, or conditions.
- Macro includes such as `#include BAD_HEADER` and include path traversal are
  not checked.
- Includes inside block comments may produce false positives.

## Third-party manifest

`third_party.toml` lists approved libraries under `[libraries.<directory>]`.
Adding a library requires maintainer approval. Each entry records `upstream`, `version`,
SPDX `license`, exact `headers`, and `allowed_prefixes`. Its `files` table maps
relative file names to their retrieval `url` and `sha256`. Files are vendored
unchanged; unexpected files, missing files, symlinks and hash mismatches fail.
GGML alone delegates verification to `check_ggml_origin.py`.

Portal is the reference CLI and its HTTP server in `tools/cli/` (C++ namespace
`portal`). Native `src/` and `include/` cannot use Portal dependencies regardless of manifest
prefixes. Portal sources and CLI unit tests may include existing Portal private
headers, but cannot include native implementation headers. Other public consumers
cannot include Portal private headers. Vendored directories are excluded from
source traversal and checked against their hashes instead.

## Example App dependencies

`app_dependencies.toml` records approved direct dependencies separately from
`third_party.toml`. Adding or replacing a library, or changing its major version,
requires maintainer approval. Patch adjustments must update the manifest in the same commit.
`check_app_deps.py` compares npm and Cargo declarations and direct lockfile resolutions,
the Android version catalog and wrapper, and Swift package declarations. npm versions
must be exact; Cargo versions use `=VERSION`. Compose UI and Material 3 inherit the
registered Compose BOM (`bom` in the allowlist). Android build scripts use catalog
aliases, not literal dependency coordinates. iOS has no third-party packages.

App directories that do not exist yet are skipped during staged implementation;
once present, their dependency manifests and lockfiles are required. Generated
directories are excluded by the shared traversal. Run the check with:

```sh
uv run --no-project python -I tools/checks/check_app_deps.py .
```

## Example App design tokens

`check_app_tokens.py` keeps colors in each App's single design-token file:
`examples/desktop/src/theme.css`, Android `ui/theme/Tokens.kt` and
`examples/ios/App/Tokens.swift`. It scans desktop `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}`,
Android `app/src/main/kotlin/**/*.kt` and iOS `App/**/*.swift`, skipping the token
files and unit test files. It reports file, line and rule for hex colors (`#rgb`,
`#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`), `rgb(`, `rgba(`, `hsl(`, `hsla(`, `Color(0x` and
`Color(red:`, `UIColor(red:`, `NSColor(red:`. `transparent`, `currentColor`, CSS
variables and platform semantic colors are allowed. Run it with:

```sh
uv run --no-project python -I tools/checks/check_app_tokens.py .
```

revision.body:
## Tickets

Addresses the cleanup and test-style review in this PR.

### What has been done

Close the operation-local Pinecone index clients after insert, search, single-record read, and gallery read, including request errors and empty results. Close the control-plane client when the adapter is explicitly closed, while accepting legacy clients that have no control-plane close method. Public operations continue to leave caller-owned control-plane clients open.

Rebased onto master at `c2a6fd9`, including #1753, #1758, and #1760. The current-SDK listing-page handling from #1753 and the maintainer's replacement tests from #1760 are retained.

Replace the former loopback-service tests with `unittest.mock` checks for operation-local index closure, original exception propagation, early returns, successful result payloads, ownership, and legacy client compatibility. The submitted tests start no local servers.

## How to test

[Revised validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43913436340), Python 3.10 and 3.12:

- Current master: **13 failed, 2 passed** in the revised regression file.
- This change plus existing listing-page, index-name, and registration-ownership tests: **36 passed** locally.
- The validation branch contains this revision and the separate gallery cleanup revision from #1740: **84 passed** across their combined related suites in each Python environment.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: **10.00/10**; MyPy: **145 source files passed**; Black formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

```shell
DEEPFACE_BACKEND_ENGINE=onnx python -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit/test_pinecone_client_lifetime.py \
  tests/unit/test_pinecone_listing_pages.py \
  tests/unit/test_pinecone_index_names.py \
  tests/unit/test_register_connection_cleanup.py
```

The earlier native-SDK investigation remains in its separate validation history: https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43866791770
